# Third-party source inventory

Generated by `scripts/collect_third_party.py`; do not hand-edit this index or `sources.json`.

68 components · 91 unique source archives · 313,126,138 compressed bytes · 1,468,398,453 regular-file source bytes.

The Go-pruned selected engine module graph contains 59 modules; 22 occur in the union of six-platform production imports. 24 module ZIPs are additionally bound to `engine/go.sum` h1 values. All selected modules have official full upstream source archives. Unavailable module ZIPs are not represented as missing source, nor as h1-verified equivalents.

## Boundaries

Archives are inert source data, not vendoring. No downloaded source, build hook or test is run during collection or verification. Builds still use the unchanged engine module files. The component count is a top-level inventory, not a claim to enumerate every embedded upstream vendor/test asset as a separate product; those original trees and notices remain in their complete archives. Source ZIPs are complete module snapshots; upstream archives are full provider snapshots at the recorded tag/commit, without Git history. The actual JSONSchema test-suite submodule is included at its parent's pinned Gitlink commit, not at moving main.

SQLite includes both modernc's generated implementation and original SQLite 3.51.2 source. The Go archive is the version declared in engine/go.mod, not a claim about the compiler used by every binary or this review. Mage/nfpm/actionlint are complete upstream tool-source snapshots at versions pinned by CI; their separate tool-development dependency graphs, hosted Actions, browser binaries, OS SDKs, proprietary agents and model services are not this engine dependency closure or an archived CI machine.

Sonar is historical provenance, not a runtime dependency. GSAP has its own license, not MIT. The independent macOS client's fonts and SwiftTerm are not shipped here. Original root-level legal files are additionally indexed byte-for-byte for reading; this does not override licenses in embedded subtrees. Original LICENSE/NOTICE/header files remain in the archives; supplemental legal documents are under [licenses/](licenses/). See [notices](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and the [source guide](../docs/third-party.md) / [中文说明](../docs/third-party.zh.md).

## Extraction warning

Verify before inspection with `python3 scripts/check_third_party.py`. Extract only into a new directory outside the checkout with path/link safety filtering. Do not execute downloaded scripts merely to inspect source. In particular, the original nfpm test fixture `files/testdata/tree/symlinks/link1` points to `/etc/foo`; this intentionally unsafe fixture is preserved as archive data, explicitly inventoried, and never extracted by these scripts. Do not blindly unpack all tool fixtures.

## Verification and intentional updates

The JSON inventory retains original source URLs, commit/tag, archive SHA-256, sizes, file counts, license paths, submodule relationship and exceptional symlinks. Input hashes bind it to the module files, site lockfile, copied GSAP asset and tool-pinning workflows.

Run `python3 scripts/check_third_party.py` for offline integrity, selected-graph and six-target production-closure checks; Go and the existing module metadata cache are required. It does not run archived code. `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p check_third_party_test.py` exercises corruption, missing source, h1 binding, unsafe paths, LFS placeholders, submodules and legal-document checks using synthetic temporary data.

After an intentional dependency/tool-version change, review and update the collector's explicit source pins, then run `python3 scripts/collect_third_party.py --collect` (Go, gh and curl required). It reads official public sources and verified cached module ZIPs, does not install anything, and fails verification if a source gap remains. Review all provenance/license/hash changes; do not update a checksum just to silence failure.

Network record: the public Go proxy timed out, so no alternate proxy was used; canonical modernc GitLab source archives were available. SQLite's official download host hit an SSL timeout; its official GitHub mirror at the fixed version commit supplied the full original source. The official GSAP license-page snapshot was retrieved on 2026-11-15 Asia/Shanghai and is a current page snapshot, not a historically versioned license.
